chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who owns a relative (of his slave), is it permissible for him to sell her or to enslave her? He said: 'It is not suitable for him to sell her, as she is his master and his brother (in freedom); if he dies, she inherits him (freeing him) rather than his children, and he is not allowed to sell her nor to enslave her.'
ai.seo_question: Can an owner sell or keep enslaved a slave who has a free relative?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the status of a slave who possesses a free female relative (often interpreted as a mother or daughter), ruling that she becomes his 'master' (*mawla*) in the sense of entitling him to manumission, preventing the owner from selling or re-enslaving her. This ruling highlights the Shia legal principle that the presence of a free close relative creates a specific bond of *kitabah* or automatic emancipation rights, ensuring the slave's dignity and freedom are preserved within the family structure. The narration underscores the precedence of kinship ties in determining inheritance and manumission, distinguishing this status from general slavery.
